record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: In two dimensions, does every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian admit a global PEPS approximation under the spectral gap assumption alone, without any additional assumption controlling the concentration of low-energy eigenvalues near the ground-state energy?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (or finite portions thereof of arbitrary size), with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space attached to each site. Let $H = \sum_{x} h_x$ be a local Hamiltonian, meaning each $h_x$ acts non-trivially on a uniformly bounded number of sites contained in a region of uniformly bounded diameter, and the operator norms $\|h_x\|$ are uniformly bounded. Assume that $H$ is gapped: there exists a constant $\gamma > 0$, independent of system size, such that the spectral gap between the ground-state energy and the rest of the spectrum is at least $\gamma$.

A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) with bond dimension $D$ on a 2D lattice is a tensor network state obtained by placing at each site a tensor with one physical index (of dimension equal to the local Hilbert space dimension) and one virtual index of dimension $D$ for each lattice edge incident to that site, and contracting all virtual indices along edges.

Say that a family of states $\{|\psi_N\rangle\}$ on regions of size $N$ admits a global PEPS approximation if there exist PEPS $\{|\phi_N\rangle\}$ with bond dimension $D(N, \varepsilon)$ growing at most quasi-polynomially in $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$ such that $\big\| |\psi_N\rangle - |\phi_N\rangle \big\| \le \varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

Question: Does every ground state of every two-dimensional local gapped Hamiltonian (in the above sense) admit a global PEPS approximation, using only the spectral gap hypothesis and without any additional assumption controlling the density or concentration of low-energy eigenvalues near the ground-state energy?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of globally approximating ground states of 2D local gapped Hamiltonians by PEPS, under only a spectral gap assumption, appears to remain open. Existing results obtain global PEPS approximations under additional assumptions on the density of low-energy eigenvalues; a 2D area law and unconditional global PEPS approximation under the gap alone have not been established. Recent work (e.g., area laws for 2D frustration-free systems) provides only partial progress in restricted settings.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
status_evidence.snippet: Lists this as an open question about 2D global PEPS approximation under the spectral gap assumption.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: An area law for 2D frustration-free spin systems
status_evidence.snippet: Proves an area law in the restricted frustration-free 2D setting, but does not resolve general gapped 2D PEPS approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress is available in restricted 2D settings.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses unresolved structural and approximation questions for PEPS.
status_evidence.claim: Related PEPS approximation questions remain unresolved.
